question:
A retail app must generate alt-text for every product photo uploaded by sellers, so screen-reader users get a meaningful description of each image, in line with accessibility guidelines.

What should the application do?

options.text: Send each uploaded image to a multimodal model configured to produce a concise, descriptive caption suitable as alt-text, generated automatically at upload time.
Require sellers to type their own alt-text, and if a seller leaves it blank, publish the product listing with the alt-text attribute simply omitted.
Use the image's file name (for example, `IMG_04213.jpg`) as the alt-text value.
Insert the same generic placeholder text, such as "product photo," as the alt-text for every image.

explanation:
A **multimodal captioning model** can automatically generate a concise, meaningful description of the actual image content at upload time, which is exactly what accessibility guidance calls for — descriptive, image-specific alt-text without depending on every seller to write it manually.

**Why not the other options:**
- **Blank alt-text when a seller skips it** — Leaves screen-reader users with nothing at all for a large share of listings; accessibility can't depend entirely on optional manual input.
- **Using the file name** — Camera-generated file names carry no descriptive information about the image content and provide no real accessibility value.
- **A single generic placeholder for every image** — Technically fills the field but conveys no image-specific information, which fails the intent of alt-text (distinguishing what is actually in *this* photo).
